newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian domestic credits down 6.7 pct in June.
newsitem.headline: Romanian domestic credits down 6.7 pct in June.

text.p: Romania's internal credits dropped by 6.7 percent to 37.69 trillion lei at end-June after a 2.7 percent rise the previous month as credits to government fell sharply, central bank data (BNR) showed on Tuesday.
End-June domestic loans were 75.16 percent up year-on-year.

Net credits to the Romanian government dipped to 1.5 trillion lei from 5.6 trillion the previous month after the Finance Ministry raised 600 million marks from the first international bond issue in its own name earlier in June.
The State Treasury General Account had 399.9 billion lei surplus at end-June, down from 1.18 trillion the previous month, BNR data showed.

Non-government credits inched up by 0.62 percent to 36.2 trillion lei at end-June after a 3.9 percent rise the previous month as banks' lending rates eased to an annual average of 91.4 percent in June from May's 109 percent.
Hard currency credits stayed almost flat at 20.6 trillion lei but their stake in total non-government loans fell to 56.9 percent from a previous 57.5 percent, BNR data showed.
Leu credits went up by two percent to 15.59 trillion lei in June with state companies taking more than half of them and short-term loans accounting for 83.9 percent of that figure.
